editorial:
Imagine living a double life right under your own roof. You meet B, a middle-aged woman in Manchester's Moss Side who seems to have it all figured out. She is a loving mother to a son who is a bit too protective, but she also has a secret side involving other men. The movie feels very real and grounded, giving you a look at a community that usually gets ignored in big cinema. It is all about the tension of keeping your private desires hidden while trying to be the perfect parent, and you can feel the pressure building up as the story moves forward.

What really makes this work is the acting, as the chemistry between B and her son feels authentic and tense. The pacing is steady, though some might find the slow build-up a bit long. If you enjoy character studies that feel like a slice of life, you will love this. It is a great choice if you want something meaningful and honest.
endingExplained: The tension finally peaks when B's secret relationships and her son's overprotectiveness clash. You see the fallout as her two worlds collide, forcing her to face the truth about her identity. Instead of a neat bow, the ending leaves you thinking about whether she can truly be free. It wraps up by showing that family bonds are messy, and B must decide if her own happiness is worth the conflict it causes with her son.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves raw family dramas and stories about secret lives.
